slides.title: Linear Equations
bullets: Class 10 — NIOS Mathematics
Chapter 5
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome students. Today we move from polynomial expressions to EQUATIONS — first in one variable, then in two.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Identify and solve linear equations in one variable.
Translate word problems into linear equations.
Recognise that a linear equation in 2 variables is a line.
Classify a 2×2 system: unique / none / infinitely many.
Solve a 2×2 system by substitution or elimination.
slides.speaker_notes: Read each objective; ask students which they feel least sure about.

slides.title: Linear equation — one variable
bullets: Standard form: ax + b = 0 with a ≠ 0.
Variable to the FIRST power only.
No products of variables; no division by a variable.
Unique solution: x = −b/a.
slides.speaker_notes: Stress 'first power only' — that's what 'linear' means.

slides.title: Equality properties
bullets: Add the same number to both sides.
Subtract the same number.
Multiply both sides by the same NON-ZERO number.
Divide both sides by the same NON-ZERO number.
These four operations preserve the truth set.
slides.speaker_notes: Multiplication / division by zero is forbidden — collapses information.

slides.title: Worked example: solve 3(x − 2) + 4 = 2x + 1
bullets: Distribute: 3x − 6 + 4 = 2x + 1.
Combine: 3x − 2 = 2x + 1.
Move x terms left, constants right: x = 3.
Verify: LHS = 7, RHS = 7 ✓.
Always verify by substitution.
slides.speaker_notes: Walk through every step on the board; encourage students to call out the next step.

slides.title: Equations with denominators
bullets: Step 1: multiply both sides by the LCM of the denominators.
Step 2: distribute and simplify.
Step 3: isolate x.
The 'clear denominators first' move makes everything else integer arithmetic.
slides.speaker_notes: Demonstrate the move ×6 carefully — students often forget to apply it to the RHS too.

slides.title: Word problems — one variable routine
bullets: Read; identify unknown; let it be x.
Translate each sentence into algebra.
Form ONE equation in x.
Solve.
Verify and translate back into the language of the problem.
slides.speaker_notes: The translate / verify steps are where most marks are dropped — emphasise.

slides.title: Word example: consecutive odd integers sum to 75
bullets: Let smallest = x; the three are x, x + 2, x + 4.
Integers: 23, 25, 27.
slides.speaker_notes: Highlight that the smallest is x, not x − 2; consistency with the variable choice matters.

slides.title: Linear equation — two variables
bullets: Standard form: ax + by + c = 0 (a, b not both 0).
Solution = ordered pair (x, y).
Has INFINITELY MANY solutions.
Geometric picture: a STRAIGHT LINE in the xy-plane.
Plot any two solutions; join them with a line.
slides.speaker_notes: Use the line y = 2x + 1 and the points students plotted in Explore phase.

slides.title: 2×2 systems — three cases
bullets: Unique: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ — lines intersect once.
Infinitely many: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ — same line.
None: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ — parallel lines.
Apply the ratio test BEFORE solving.
It tells you which case you are in.
slides.speaker_notes: The ratio test is the workhorse for the whole 2×2 part of the chapter.

slides.title: Substitution: x + y = 7, x − y = 1
bullets: From eq.1: y = 7 − x.
Substitute into eq.2: x − (7 − x) = 1.
Solution: (4, 3).
slides.speaker_notes: When a coefficient is 1, isolate that variable — substitution is fastest.

slides.title: Elimination: 3x + 2y = 16, 5x + 2y = 22
bullets: Subtract eq.1 from eq.2: 2x = 6 → x = 3.
Substitute back: 9 + 2y = 16 → 2y = 7 → y = 7/2.
Solution: (3, 7/2).
Subtraction WORKS because y-coefficients matched.
If they don't, multiply equations to make them match.
slides.speaker_notes: Elimination is the workhorse method when neither coefficient is 1.

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 2. Solve x/3 − x/5 = 2.
3. Sum of two consecutive integers is 47. Find them.
4. Solve by substitution: x = 3y, 2x + y = 14.
5. Classify 2x + 3y = 7, 4x + 6y = 9 (use the ratio test).
slides.speaker_notes: Walk the room. Watch for sign-flip errors and incomplete distribution.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. Standard form of a linear equation in one variable?
Q2. How many solutions does ax + by + c = 0 have?
Q3. If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, how many solutions?
Q4. Which method is best when a coefficient is 1?
Show your answers on fingers.
slides.speaker_notes: Address the question with the most disagreement.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Linear = first power; no products of variables; no division by a variable.
ax + b = 0 has unique solution x = −b/a.
5-step plan: clear denominators, distribute, isolate, divide, verify.
ax + by + c = 0 → infinitely many solutions; geometrically a line.
2×2 systems: ratio test → unique / none / infinitely many.
Solve by substitution, elimination or cross-multiplication — pick the easiest fit.
slides.speaker_notes: Hand out the worksheet and announce homework.
